prerequisites: EXPRESION GRAFICA Y DISEÑO ASISTIDO POR ORDENADOR (565000315)

learning_outcomes.text: Possess the ability to design, develop, implement, manage and improve products, systems and processes in different industrial fields, using appropriate analytical, computational or experimental techniques.
Apply acquired knowledge to identify, formulate and solve problems in broad contexts, being able to integrate them working in multidisciplinary teams.
Communicate knowledge and conclusions, both orally and in writing, to specialized and non-specialized audiences clearly and unambiguously.
Possess learning skills that allow continuous lifelong study for appropriate professional development.
Incorporate ICT and Industrial Engineering technologies and tools into their professional activities.
Know and apply basic science and technology knowledge to the practice of Industrial Engineering.
Knowledge and capacities to apply graphic engineering techniques.
Ability to design, use and model mechanical systems using a current parametric computer-aided design tool.
Ability to produce and interpret technical graphic documentation.
Ability to sketch mechanical parts and assemblies.

syllabus_topics: Drawings for different technical areas in engineering
Standardized perspectives. Dimetric and cavalier perspective
Characteristics, use, representation and standardized designation of elements used in removable joints
Characteristics, use, representation and standardized designation of elements used against rotation
Chains and belts: Elements, classification and representation
Introduction and definitions of dimensional tolerances
Representation of dimensional tolerances and fits in the drawing
Indication of general dimensional tolerance in the drawing
Symbols and indication in the drawing
Indication of general surface finish in the drawing
Symbols and indication in the drawings
Indication of general geometric tolerance in the drawings
GRAPHIC DOCUMENTATION IN PROJECTS AND INSTALLATIONS
assessment_rules: The final grade is on a scale of 0 to 10 points, with a minimum of 5 points required to pass. A minimum grade of 4.0 points out of 10 in the global exam is required for other blocks to be computed; otherwise, the maximum final grade for the course will be 4.0 points. Grades of 5.0 or higher in sketching, theory assignments, and CAD lab work can be carried over to future academic years if the study plan does not change. For the extraordinary call, grades from sketching, theory assignments, and CAD lab work obtained during the course will be maintained, and no re-evaluation will be offered for these blocks.
